subject: PMTU failures over customer GRE/IP-in-IP tunnel — packet fragmentation on large payloads
messages:
From: Sylvia Gomez <sylvia@cloudline.io>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T18:12:00Z
Subject: Intermittent failures on on-prem GRE tunnel (large uploads)

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing failed uploads from our on-prem app to Redwood Private yesterday evening. Small files succeed, large TAR uploads fail mid-way and the client shows ECONNRESET. We captured traffic and see ICMP unreachable (fragmentation needed) coming back from an intermediate hop, but our firewall is set to allow ICMP. This is over a GRE tunnel you've provisioned to our edge.

Short summary:
- Affected flow: src 10.4.8.0/24 -> dst 172.22.0.0/23 (customers -> private deployment)
- Observed: retransmits and occasional path MTU blackhole (ICMP type 3 code 4 seen intermittently)
- Time window: 2027-05-11 17:30–19:00 UTC

Attached: packet_capture_20270511.pcap, route_table_snapshot.txt

Can you help triage? We suspect tunnel encapsulation is reducing MTU and something along the path is dropping fragmented packets or clearing DF.

Thanks,
Sylvia
Sr. NetEng, Cloudline

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T18:29:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent failures on on-prem GRE tunnel (large uploads)

Soojin / Connor — forwarding Cloudline's capture. They report ICMP fragmentation-needed intermittently.

Quick context: this is the private deployment tunnel between our VPC edge (10.100.12.0/24) and Cloudline's colocation via GRE (we use IP-in-IP for backup). We recently pushed an update changing the tunnel type to keepalive-probe on and adjusted PMTU discovery settings at the edge last month (ticket NETOPS-7892). If this is a PMTU blackhole, likely causes:
- MTU mismatch on intermediate carrier devices after encapsulation (GRE + IP headers)
- DF bit being propagated and fragmented packets dropped by a firewall or NAT in the path
- Our tunnel endpoint not clamping MSS on TCP SYNs

Can you triage the capture and check edge iptables mangle rules, sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing, and whether ipip/gre adds the expected overhead? If we need an immediate mitigation, let's test an iptables TCPMSS clamp on the egress interface or temporarily lower the GRE MTU.

I'll loop in Marissa for priority and customer comms.

Thanks — Lauren
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T19:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: Intermittent failures on on-prem GRE tunnel (large uploads)

I pulled the pcap and did a quick check. Observations:
- I see SYN packets from client with MSS 1460; after GRE (encapsulation adds ~24 bytes for GRE+IP) the packets exceed our physical link MTU of 1500 and the DF bit is set.
- There are ICMP type 3 code 4 messages from hop 10.254.3.1 back to the tunnel egress, reporting next-hop MTU 1380. Not all flows deliver ICMP consistently (classic PMTU discovery intermittency).
- Cloudline's firewall appears to drop fragmented non-first fragments on return path; they confirmed a tighter frag policy on some appliances.

Immediate remediations I tested in staging:
- Enabling iptables mangle TCPMSS clamp on the tunnel egress interface:
  iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
  This rewrites MSS in SYN and prevents endpoints from sending > PMTU.
- sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 (aggressively probes) helps for in-flight sessions but not for established long uploads; better for new sessions.
- Alternative: set the GRE interface mtu to 1400 on the edge endpoints to force lower frames through encapsulation.

Risk/notes:
- MSS clamp is low risk but interacts with clients doing MSS-less TCP stacks (rare).
- Lowering GRE MTU will increase fragmentation overhead for small frames inside encapsulation, may impact throughput slightly.

Next steps: I propose we apply TCPMSS clamp on the VPC edge in staging and then to production during a low-impact window (we can roll back quickly). Connor, can you check that our edge routing/NAT boxes will not rewrite MSS or tamper with TCP options? Also confirm there are no iptables conntrack helpers that could be affected.

I'll prepare a short runbook.

— Soojin
Network Reliability Engineer

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sylvia Gomez <sylvia@cloudline.io>
Date: 2027-05-12T02:17:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: Intermittent failures on on-prem GRE tunnel (large uploads)

Thanks all — I validated the route snapshots. Quick notes from edge boxes (output attached in ipsec_status.log):
- GRE interface gre0 on edge1: mtu 1500 (default)
- Underlay physical interface eth0: mtu 1500
- No mangle TCPMSS rules currently on FORWARD chain for that tunnel; NAT is done on the egress box but conntrack is in default mode.
- There are no middleboxes in our VPC that would intentionally drop ICMP, but the upstream carrier (10.254.3.1) is signaling MTU 1380 intermittently.

I applied the iptables mangle rule in a controlled staging route for Cloudline's tenant and re-ran the same transfer test they did. Result: large uploads completed end-to-end without resets. I rolled back after verification.

Suggested plan for production (short window):
1) Schedule 30-min maintenance window 2027-05-12 03:00–03:30 UTC (low traffic).
2) Apply: iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on edge devices and persist via config management.
3) Set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on edge hosts.
4) Monitor Cloudline's flows and packet drops for 1 hour.
5) If issues persist, set gre0 mtu to 1400 as secondary mitigation (requires coordinating with Cloudline for symmetric MTU).

Sylvia — can you confirm whether Cloudline can temporarily permit fragments on return path for troubleshooting and whether they can lower their host-side MTU for a quick test? If they prefer, we can do the MSS clamp first and see if that resolves.

I'm leaving a note in Jira NETOPS-8421.

— Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Sylvia Gomez <sylvia@cloudline.io>, Etienne Moreau <etienne@cloudline.io>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures on on-prem GRE tunnel (large uploads)

Sylvia / Etienne —

Thanks for the prompt capture and logs. Summary of what we did and recommended next steps:
- Root cause: PMTU discovery intermittently failing because GRE/IP-in-IP encapsulation reduces effective MTU; upstream hop sometimes reports MTU 1380 and Cloudline's appliance drops non-first fragments on the return path.
- Immediate mitigation applied in staging: TCP MSS clamping on SYN prevents endpoints from sending segments that exceed the effective PMTU; staging tests succeeded.

Proposed production action (pending your confirmation):
1) We will apply MSS clamp on our edge during a short maintenance window (2027-05-12 03:00–03:30 UTC). This should be transparent to apps and resolve your upload failures without requiring changes from your side.
2) We'll also enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 to accelerate PMTU correction for new flows.
3) If you can temporarily allow fragmented packets on the return path or lower host MTU for a 10-minute test that will help confirm the full path behavior; not required but useful for root-cause verification.

Please reply with which option you prefer. If you approve the maintenance window, we'll proceed and send a confirmation once done.

Thanks,
Lauren
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference
